description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:763-765 — ValidatedPath.depth doc comment:
  'Note: this counts all certificates except the trust anchor — including self-issued intermediates that RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9 excludes from the pathLenConstraint count. For chains with self-issued intermediates the depth field may be larger than the RFC 5280 path length.'

This is correctly documented. However in validate_path, depth is set as:
  `depth: chain.len().saturating_sub(1)`

For a chain [leaf, int], depth = 1. For [leaf, int, self_issued_int], depth = 2. The pathLenConstraint check uses num_non_si_intermediates which excludes self-issued. These are intentionally different metrics.

The depth field is used in tests (e.g., ValidatedPath::depth == 1 in two_cert_chain_ok). If a caller uses depth to compare against a pathLenConstraint they copied from a certificate, they'd get the wrong answer.

P3 — the doc comment is correct but the dual semantics (raw chain depth vs RFC 5280 path length) may confuse callers. Add a cross-reference in ValidatedPath.depth doc to the distinction. No code bug.
title: pkix-path doc: ValidatedPath depth field counts ALL intermediates including self-issued
